observed_behavior: A naive credential pattern for the 'sk-' key prefix matched ordinary words containing that substring, such as 'task-completion'. The detector therefore produced false positives on benign engineering text, which erodes trust in the control and invites disabling it.
principle: Credential detection over free text requires an explicit token boundary and a minimum secret length, because a bare prefix substring match fires inside ordinary words and a detector that cries wolf gets switched off, which is a worse security outcome than the false positives it was added to prevent.
trigger: implementing or reviewing credential/secret detection over free text
verified_correction: Credential detection requires an explicit token boundary. The supervisor screen uses an anchored pattern with a word boundary and a minimum key length rather than a bare substring test.

observed_behavior: A pattern-based process kill issued from a shell whose own command line contained the pattern matched the issuing shell itself, terminating the controlling session along with the intended target.
principle: When terminating a process by command-line pattern, the issuing shell's own command line is part of the match space, so prefer a recorded PID or a service unit over a broad pattern, because a self-matching kill removes the session that would otherwise observe and repair the damage.
trigger: terminating a process by command-line pattern from a shell session
verified_correction: Target processes by an identifier that cannot match the issuing session — a recorded PID, a service unit, or a pattern anchored to the specific executable — rather than by a broad command-line substring.
